one_line: A 10-second photoreal AI clip of a golden-retriever puppy and a baby in a yellow romper sitting on a sofa, ending with the baby leaning in to touch noses with the puppy.

hook.visual: Locked-off vertical shot of a puppy and a baby in a yellow sleeveless romper sitting side by side on a beige sofa, facing each other, the puppy's nose almost touching the baby's cheek at 0.0 s.
hook.on_screen_text: none except a moving 'Sora' watermark (top-left at 0.0 to 2.0 s). (No caption text burned in.)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Observed: two baby-faced subjects at eye level with almost no distance between their faces at 0.0 s, and the baby stares at the puppy without moving. Inferred: the near-touch sets up a 'will they touch' question with no text needed, and the content works with no language.

beats.observed: Puppy leans its muzzle toward the baby's face at 0.0 s, then sits upright looking forward by 2.0 s. Baby sits still in the yellow romper and watches the puppy.
beats.spoken: No speech. Whisper tags only '(dog barking)' from 0.0 to 2.5 s.

beats.observed: Baby raises the right hand with fingers spread toward the puppy at 3.0 s, then lowers it to the chest at 4.0 s. Puppy stays upright, looking off-frame.
beats.on_screen_text: 'Sora' watermark moves to the baby's torso at 3.0 to 4.0 s

beats.observed: Both hold still. Baby clasps hands in lap and looks at the puppy's face. Puppy keeps its head up and turned slightly away.
Baby's gaze is fixed on the puppy; hands in lap. Puppy turns its head slightly toward the baby.
Baby leans the whole upper body forward toward the puppy's nose while legs and feet stay planted.
Baby's nose touches the puppy's nose at 8.0 s and the contact holds at 9.0 s. Last second (9.0 to 10.0 s) not sampled.
beats.on_screen_text: 'Sora' watermark top-left at 8.0 s, on the baby's arm at 9.0 s

payoff: The nose-to-nose touch between baby and puppy, first visible at 8.0 s and still holding at 9.0 s (about 80 to 90 percent of the way through the clip).
cta: Caption: 'Drop a 🐾 if this one's highlight reel material 👇' (a one-emoji comment prompt).
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: a baby and a puppy touching noses is easy to send to a partner or parent in one tap, and the one-emoji comment ask takes no effort. No text or language barrier.
why_it_worked: 286,839,984 views is 2,462x the account's median of 116,500 (meta.json), so this clip is a rare breakout on an account that normally lands near 100K. Inferred: a Shorts feed spike, not the format alone.
2,403,189 likes at a 0.84% like rate is a broad, genuine-looking reaction, not a thin-engagement paid pattern.
Observed: one shot, one gesture, no text, payoff at 8 s of a 10 s clip, so almost nobody needs to leave before the touch. Inferred high completion; no retention data in meta.json.
paid_signal: no, inferred: like_rate 0.84% is above the 0.3% threshold for suspected paid reach, and a Shorts feed breakout explains the numbers. Cannot verify.

solo_route.how: 1) Take one of LumeBook's own illustrated child-hero images (side view, sitting) as the first-frame still. 2) Run it through an image-to-video tool for 8 to 10 s with a one-action prompt: puppy sniffs, hero looks, hero leans in, noses touch. Generate 6 to 10 takes and keep the one where hands and body do not glitch. 3) Add no text for the first 8 s. In the last 1.5 s add a small Hebrew line from LumeBook, and put a one-emoji comment prompt in the caption. Total length 8 to 10 s. About 1 to 2 hours including retries. Do not ship a photoreal baby: keep LumeBook's illustrated look so the clip sells the product.
solo_route.needs: Nothing external for a generic illustrated hero. Check the AI tool's terms for commercial use and for a watermark-free export (this video shows a moving 'Sora' watermark, which looks off-brand on a LumeBook post). Add the platform's AI-content label.

lumebook_version.hook_he: גור פוגש את גיבור הספר. מה קורה בשנייה 8?
lumebook_version.concept: One locked-off 8 to 10 second image-to-video of LumeBook's illustrated child hero and a puppy sidekick on a sofa, no text until the final nose-touch, ending on a title card that says the hero can be your own child.

evidence_notes: AI cues observed in frames: the baby's skin is very smooth with no pores or fine texture; the baby's hair is a uniform soft fuzz; the puppy's fur is smooth with few individual strands; at 3.0 s the raised hand has spread, slightly smeared fingers; at 7.0 s the baby's torso leans forward while legs and feet stay planted and the shoulder outline shifts without a visible weight shift. No identity morphing was seen between frames, but sampling was one frame per second, so changes inside a second cannot be ruled out. Tool: the on-screen text 'Sora' appears as a moving watermark (top-left at 0.0 to 2.0 s, on the baby's torso at 3.0 to 4.0 s, bottom-left at 5.0 to 6.0 s, top-left at 7.0 to 8.0 s, on the baby's arm at 9.0 s). Inferred: the clip was generated or exported with the Sora app; the watermark does not prove who made it. The caption names no tool, only the hashtag #aibaby. Transcript: Whisper gives only '(dog barking)' for 0.0 to 2.5 s, but the puppy's mouth is closed in the frames at 0.0, 1.0 and 2.0 s, so the sound is not visibly matched to the picture (I cannot hear it). Inferred: the audio was added or generated separately. made_by brand_inhouse means only that the account posted it; I cannot tell whether the account generated the clip or re-uploaded it. Likeness and consent: nothing in the frames or caption suggests a real child's photo was used, but this cannot be verified. Risk for LumeBook: a photoreal fake baby sits against its own 'your real child' promise, and platforms ask for AI labels on realistic synthetic content. Never feed a customer's child photo into a public ad without written parental consent.
